newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Modelo Q4 results seen steady.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Modelo Q4 results seen steady.

text.p: Beverage analysts expect more of the same from leading Mexican brewer Grupo Modelo when Q4 earnings are reported: another healthy quarter fueled by strong exports, aggressive marketing and improved distribution.
That's pretty much been the Modelo story since it went public in 1994.
The average forecast of three analysts consulted by Reuters predicted earnings per share of 1.44 pesos compared with 1.24 pesos in 1995. Modelo is expected to report in late February.

The average forecast of the operating margin is 20.47 percent against 17.6 percent in 1995, with the margin likely to skyrocket in the fourth quarter over the same period in 1995 because of a change in Modelo's accounting methods.
Sales volumes are seen up anywhere from 5.0 percent to 7.5 percent in the domestic market and in a range of 26 percent to 28 percent for exports.
Modelo's exports were up 30.6 percent for the first nine months of the year but tend to slow in the fourth quarter, when colder temperatures in the United States reduce beer demand.

"The distributors this year have really tried to attack new markets, and it's worked," said Thomas Mobille, a Latin American beer analyst for Robert Fleming in Brazil. "The growth in the traditional markets is good as it is, but now they're benefitting from better distribution in new (U.S.) states."
Mobille said growing exports in far-flung places like Europe, Asia and Israel are starting to show up more on Modelo's bottom line.
But that will be tempered by the stronger Mexican peso, another analyst said.
"The thing is with the stronger peso we'll see that the exports are not going to help the operating margin as much as they did the past two years," said Raul Romano of BBV-Probursa in Mexico City.
